brief:
Israeli settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank is propelled by both ideological commitment and economic incentives, Al Jazeera English reported. The growth reflects a dual motivation among Israeli settlers who move to the territory for reasons beyond political conviction alone.

Housing subsidies, tax breaks, and employment opportunities constitute significant financial attractions that encourage Israeli citizens to relocate to settlements. These economic benefits work alongside ideological factors rooted in territorial and historical claims. The combination of financial incentives and political ideology has shaped the trajectory and distribution of settlement construction across the West Bank over time.
dek: Israeli settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank isn’t just driven by ideology, but also by economic incentives.
title: Economic incentives drive Israeli West Bank settlement expansion
